screen.description: The root of every document: one full screen of UI, carrying the format version.

weft.description: The Weft format version of the document: "0.2", or "0.1" for a document written before 0.2.

stack.description: Lays its children out in one line, as a column or a row; use it for most vertical or horizontal grouping.

direction.description: Whether children flow down a column or along a row.

gap.description: Space between children, as a dimension token.

align.description: How children are aligned across the main direction.

justify.description: How free space along the main direction is shared: after, around or before the children, or between them.

wrap.description: Set to true to let children wrap onto further lines when they do not fit.

padding.description: Inner spacing on all four sides of the stack, as a dimension token.

max-width.description: Widest the stack may be, as a dimension token; it fills its parent up to that width.

material.description: Frosted-glass surface behind the stack, as a material token: a background blur and a tint.

grid.description: Lays its children out in a fixed number of equal columns; use it for card galleries and dashboards.

columns.description: Number of equal columns in the grid, at least 1.

gap.description: Space between grid cells, as a dimension token.

min-column-width.description: Narrowest a column may be, as a dimension token; below it the grid shows fewer columns, down to one.

padding.description: Inner spacing on all four sides of the grid, as a dimension token.

max-width.description: Widest the grid may be, as a dimension token; it fills its parent up to that width.

material.description: Frosted-glass surface behind the grid, as a material token: a background blur and a tint.

section.description: A named region of the screen that groups related content; use it to divide a screen into labelled parts.

header.description: Optional header content shown above the section body, such as a heading.

heading.description: A title for the content that follows it; the level orders headings from 1 (most important) to 6.

level.description: Heading level from 1 to 6; use 1 for the screen title.

text.description: The text to show, given as a value instead of content; bind it when the text comes from data. Never give both.
A run of plain text such as a paragraph, caption or message.

tone.description: Semantic colouring of the text; muted for secondary text, danger for errors.

text.description: The text to show, given as a value instead of content; bind it when the text comes from data. Never give both.

image.description: A picture; always give a label that describes it for people who cannot see it.

src.description: Where the image is loaded from, a URL or a binding to one.

model.description: A 3D model the user can turn; give it a still fallback image and a label that describes what it shows.

src.description: The glTF binary or JSON file (.glb, .gltf) the web shows; a path relative to the project or an https URL, never a binding.

usdz.description: The USDZ file (.usdz) Apple platforms show; a path relative to the project or an https URL, never a binding.

fallback.description: A still image (.png, .jpg, .jpeg, .webp) shown while the model loads, where it cannot be shown, and in design tools; same path rules as src.

link.description: Navigates to another place; use a button instead for actions that change data.

href.description: The destination URL; leave it out when navigation is handled by `on-press`.

text.description: The text to show, given as a value instead of content; bind it when the text comes from data. Never give both.

button.description: Triggers an action when pressed; use it for submitting, confirming and other commands.

variant.description: Visual emphasis: primary for the main action, danger for destructive ones.

disabled.description: Set to true to make the button non-interactive.

submit.description: Set to true to make the button submit its enclosing form, firing the form's `submit` event; such a button needs no `on-press`.

text.description: The text to show, given as a value instead of content; bind it when the text comes from data. Never give both.

form.description: Groups input controls that are submitted together; the `submit` event fires when the user submits it.

footer.description: Actions of the form, typically the submit and cancel buttons.

field.description: A single-value text input such as an email, password, number or multi-line note.

type.description: What kind of text is entered; it selects the keyboard and masking.

value.description: The current text; bind it to a path to read and write the input.

placeholder.description: Hint text shown while the field is empty; it does not replace the label.

required.description: Set to true when the user must fill the field in.

disabled.description: Set to true to make the field non-interactive.

error.description: An error message to show for this field; set it when the value is invalid.

checkbox.description: A box the user ticks or clears to turn one independent option on or off.

checked.description: Whether the control is on; bind it to a boolean to read and write it.

disabled.description: Set to true to make the checkbox non-interactive.

switch.description: A toggle that applies a setting immediately; prefer it over a checkbox for on/off settings.

checked.description: Whether the control is on; bind it to a boolean to read and write it.

disabled.description: Set to true to make the switch non-interactive.

radio-group.description: A set of radio options of which exactly one can be chosen.

value.description: The `value` of the selected radio; bind it to read and write the choice.

radio.description: One choice inside a radio group; its content is the visible label.

value.description: The value the group takes when this radio is selected.

disabled.description: Set to true to make this choice non-interactive.

text.description: The text to show, given as a value instead of content; bind it when the text comes from data. Never give both.

select.description: A drop-down that lets the user choose one option from a longer list.

value.description: The `value` of the chosen option; bind it to read and write the choice.

disabled.description: Set to true to make the select non-interactive.

option.description: One choice inside a select or combobox; its content is the visible text.

value.description: The value the select or combobox takes when this option is chosen.

text.description: The text to show, given as a value instead of content; bind it when the text comes from data. Never give both.

combobox.description: A text input with suggested options, for a value the user may type or pick; use select when only the listed options are valid.

value.description: The text of the input; bind it to read and write what the user typed or picked.

placeholder.description: Hint text shown while the input is empty; it does not replace the label.

disabled.description: Set to true to make the combobox non-interactive.

slider.description: A thumb the user drags along a range to choose a number; use it when the exact value matters less than the position.

value.description: The current number; bind it to read and write the choice.

min.description: The smallest value the slider allows; the default is 0.

max.description: The largest value the slider allows; the default is 100.

step.description: The distance between values the slider moves in; the default is 1.

disabled.description: Set to true to make the slider non-interactive.

stepper.description: A number the user raises or lowers by a fixed step with plus and minus buttons; use it for small counts such as a quantity.

value.description: The current number; bind it to read and write the count.

min.description: The smallest value the stepper allows; without it the value has no lower bound.

max.description: The largest value the stepper allows; without it the value has no upper bound.

step.description: The amount one press adds or subtracts; the default is 1.

disabled.description: Set to true to make the stepper non-interactive.

date-picker.description: Chooses a date, a time or both; the value is written as text in a fixed format.

type.description: What is chosen: `date` as yyyy-mm-dd, `time` as hh:mm, `datetime` as yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm.

value.description: The chosen date or time in the format of `type`; bind it to read and write it.

min.description: The earliest allowed value, in the format of `type`.

max.description: The latest allowed value, in the format of `type`.

disabled.description: Set to true to make the picker non-interactive.

color-picker.description: Chooses a colour; the value is written as a lowercase hex colour such as #3b82f6.

value.description: The chosen colour as #rrggbb; bind it to read and write the choice.

disabled.description: Set to true to make the colour picker non-interactive.

segmented-control.description: A row of joined segments of which exactly one can be chosen; use it for a few short, mutually exclusive choices that switch a view or mode.

value.description: The `value` of the chosen segment; bind it to read and write the choice.

segment.description: One choice inside a segmented control; its content is the visible text.

value.description: The value the control takes when this segment is chosen.

disabled.description: Set to true to make this segment non-interactive.

text.description: The text to show, given as a value instead of content; bind it when the text comes from data. Never give both.

list.description: A sequence of items; use it for feeds and collections, with `ordered` when the order matters.

ordered.description: Set to true when the order of the items is meaningful.

empty.description: Content shown instead of the items when there are none, such as "No results found".

item.description: One entry of a list; it can hold text and other components and may be pressed.

text.description: The text to show, given as a value instead of content; bind it when the text comes from data. Never give both.

table.description: Tabular data with column headers and rows; always give it a label.

empty.description: Content shown instead of the rows when there are none, such as "No results found".

column.description: A column header of a table; its content is the header text.

sort.description: The sort direction currently applied to this column.

text.description: The text to show, given as a value instead of content; bind it when the text comes from data. Never give both.

row.description: One row of a table, made of cells in the order of the columns.

selected.description: Set to true when the row is selected.

cell.description: One data cell of a table row; it can hold text and other components.

text.description: The text to show, given as a value instead of content; bind it when the text comes from data. Never give both.

tabs.description: Switches between alternative panels, one visible at a time; each panel is a `tab` child.

selected.description: The `id` of the selected `tab`; bind it to read and write the active tab.

tab.description: One panel of a tabs component: its label becomes the tab title and its content the panel.

dialog.description: A window above the screen for confirmations and short tasks; put its buttons in `actions`.

modal.description: When true the rest of the screen is blocked while the dialog is open.

open.description: Whether the dialog is shown; bind it to read and write visibility.

actions.description: The buttons that answer the dialog, such as Cancel and Confirm.

alert.description: A message that tells the user about a result or problem, announced to assistive technology.

text.description: The text to show, given as a value instead of content; bind it when the text comes from data. Never give both.

menu.description: A list of commands the user can pick from, such as an actions or overflow menu.

menu-item.description: One command inside a menu; its content is the visible text.

disabled.description: Set to true to make the command non-interactive.

text.description: The text to show, given as a value instead of content; bind it when the text comes from data. Never give both.
